source_1_night_watcher.summary: Repeated transfer re-submission observed unchanged valid project state until an empty path/namespace response appeared; system must preserve last valid identity, detect no progress, bound retries, persist evidence, and stop safely.

source_2_copilot_repository_analysis.summary: RepositoryRepairController is the authoritative repair lifecycle; false completion must be evidence-gated and live Groq tool requests must distinguish tool-capable vs non-tool payloads.

source_3_barrot_requirements.summary: Autonomy requires audit, repair planning, mutation, validation, commit creation, remote verification, evidence persistence, queue advancement gating, and safe resume.

agreements: Completion must be gated by concrete evidence rather than loop exhaustion or status-file writes.
Durable state and explicit failure classification are required for safe autonomous resume.
Remote verification and machine-readable collaboration evidence are mandatory before advancing work.
contradictions_resolved: The repository had durable repair-cycle evidence but not durable external project identity for queue orchestration.
The live Groq request path could surface a tool conflict without normalized classification in the final queue outcome.
missing_capabilities_closed: Preservation of last valid project identity across invalid external observations.
Bounded observe-only retry/backoff instead of repeated identical submissions.
Durable work-queue persistence with explicit blocked/retry-exhausted outcomes.
Queue advancement gating on verified repair completion and optional verified sync completion.
duplicated_capabilities_avoided: Night-Watcher handling was consolidated into the existing RepositoryRepairController ecosystem instead of creating a parallel repair implementation.
unsafe_assumptions_removed: Empty path/namespace observations can no longer overwrite a known-valid project identity.
Unchanged external state no longer implies progress or justify infinite re-submission.

actions_performed: Kept RepositoryRepairController as the authoritative repair engine and added durable Night-Watcher orchestration around it.
Added ProjectIdentity validation/preservation logic for path_with_namespace and namespace state.
Added SyncController with bounded retries, observe-only backoff, invalid-response blocking, and structured attempt evidence.
Added DurableWorkStore and WorkQueueController to persist work state, resume safely, and prevent queue advancement after failed repair.
Rewired scripts/barrot_agent.py main() through WorkQueueController and expanded collaboration-record emission.
Extended tests to cover preserved project identity, invalid empty responses, bounded retries, resume, queue gating, and persisted sync evidence.

tests.details: Completed with one pre-existing SyntaxWarning in barrot_agent/tools/upgrade_bundle.py

results.repair_controller: RepositoryRepairController remains authoritative for audit, planning, patching, validation, commit creation, remote verification, and completion gating.
results.queue_orchestration: WorkQueueController persists durable work evidence, safe resume metadata, and blocks queue advancement unless repair completes successfully.
results.external_state_integrity: SyncController preserves the last valid project identity, records invalid empty observations, applies bounded backoff, and terminates in BLOCKED instead of looping indefinitely.
results.llm_tool_conflict: Live Groq tool/non-tool request handling remains normalized so tool conflicts are classified as LLM_TOOL_CONFLICT and cannot produce COMPLETE.
